results.evidence: The contradiction is real: waypoints, approach_logistics, road, access, approach and descent_text use Whiskey Bend and the Elwha Snowfinger, while all six itinerary days, itinerary.cal and timing.sectionBreakdown run a Sol Duc/High Divide/Catwalk trip. No external source describes an approach specifically to Mount Dana; Wikipedia and PeakVisor only place it in the Bailey Range draining to the Elwha (47.7913,-123.4859, Mount Norton 6.3 km SE), which puts it well east of the main Bailey crest and ~5 mi east of Dodwell-Rixon Pass, so even the Elwha/Dodwell-Rixon line in the row is doubtful. Fixing it means rewriting the entire 6-day itinerary and timing (titles, notes, miles, gain/loss, hours) with no sourced figures, so no patch is written.

gain_ft 5414 (and loss_ft 5414) disagree with the itinerary sums (14,400 gain / 15,800 loss) and the totalNote's 14,000-16,000 ft. No outside source states a car-to-car gain or loss for Mount Dana by any approach, and the itinerary itself describes a different trailhead (see the trailhead contradiction), so neither figure can be confirmed.

results.correct_value: about 7 miles each way from Madison Falls to Whiskey Bend
results.evidence: The NPS Whiskey Bend trailhead page gives 6.9 mi total walking up the road from Madison Falls. A trail-running route description gives 0.7 mi of paved road, the bypass trail, ~0.8 mi more to Whiskey Bend Road, then the 4.5 mi Whiskey Bend Road (about 7 mi total); another guide calls it a ~6.5 mi road/trail route. The ~8 mi on the trailhead card is the outlier; approach, access.closures and road.driveNote already say ~7.

results.correct_value: Permits are created through Recreation.gov, by phone with the WIC, or in person at a WIC; no same-day walk-ups are held; cross-country trips (e.g. Bailey Range) cannot be booked online and must be arranged by calling the WIC.
results.evidence: The NPS wilderness reservations page says all permits are created through Recreation.gov, can be arranged by phone or in person at a WIC, no sites are held as same-day walk-ups, and cross-country trips such as the Bailey Range must be booked by contacting the WIC at (360) 565-3100. Campflare independently states cross-country trips (e.g. Bailey Range) must be booked through the WIC by phone. The three channels are not contradictory in general, but access.permit and itinerary.cal present Recreation.gov/quota booking as the route's channel although its high nights are in cross-country zones, so both get the phone requirement; bivy is not touched.
